US to Build Two Military Bases in Greenland Under New Defense Deal

The United States will establish two new military bases in Greenland as part of a new defense agreement with Denmark. This deal expands upon a 1951 agreement, prioritizing the role of the U.S. military, Greenland's sovereignty, environmental protection, and territorial integrity. The stated aim of the agreement is to bring peace, security, and stability to the Arctic region. The deal was signed at the UN General Assembly.
